## Epic

#124 Next.js presentation foundation and incremental Streamlit migration

## User story

As a user, I want a list of past chats and the ability to open one and continue from where I left off so New chat does not permanently discard earlier conversations.

## Context

Today Next.js keeps a **single** browser transcript under `kernector:chat-messages:v1` (`web/lib/runtime-settings-storage.ts`). New chat clears that key. Ask already accepts turn `history` for multi-turn within the active transcript (#235). There is no conversation list or resume path.

This is **not** LangGraph agent memory (#213). Export of a conversation remains #243.

## Exact scope

- Introduce a client-local multi-conversation model (thread id, title/preview, updated-at, messages) — e.g. versioned localStorage or equivalent — migrating or superseding the single-key transcript safely.
- Chat UI: list past conversations, open one into the thread, start **New chat** without deleting others, continue ask turns on the selected thread (reuse existing `/api/v1/chat/ask` + `history`).
- Rename/delete conversation (minimum viable; confirm destructive deletes with `ConfirmDialog`).
- Document the storage key/schema version and migration from `kernector:chat-messages:v1`.
- Offline/unit tests for storage + UI selection/resume; keep architecture boundaries (no server auth requirement in v1).

## Exclusions

- Server-side / multi-device sync (likely needs #182 later)
- LangGraph checkpoint / long-term agent memory (#213)
- Chat visual polish-only work (separate UX ticket)
- JSON/CSV/PDF export (#243) beyond what history selection might later feed
- Rewriting grounded-ask domain logic

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] User can see a list of past conversations and open one to view its transcript.
- [ ] User can send a new ask turn on an opened conversation and it appends to that thread (history sent correctly).
- [ ] New chat creates a fresh thread without wiping other saved conversations.
- [ ] User can delete (and optionally rename) a conversation with clear confirmation where destructive.
- [ ] Existing single-transcript localStorage migrates into the multi-thread store without data loss when possible.
- [ ] Tests cover storage migration, list/open/new/delete, and resume ask path without live model calls.

## Dependencies

- Parent epic **#124**
- Builds on closed chat parity **#235**
- Related later: auth/personalisation **#182** for server-backed history
- Distinct from **#213** (agent memory) and Chat UX polish ticket

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Multi-conversation history usable in Next.js Chat
- [ ] Storage versioning + migration documented
- [ ] Tests green; no architecture boundary regressions
title: Chat history: list, open, and continue past conversations

## Context

- Improve Chat layout and hierarchy under Instrument panel (ADR 0003): empty state, thread readability, composer focus, sticky/send affordances, spacing density.
- Clarify **New chat** vs continuing the current transcript (copy and placement), without introducing a conversation list.
- Tighten loading / error / unavailable states for scanability; keep sanitized Problem Details messaging.
- Small a11y and keyboard wins on composer and primary actions (focus order, labels, live region behavior if needed).
- Keep shell domain-neutral; no pack-specific chrome.

## Exclusions

- Multi-conversation list / resume past chats (follow-up history ticket)
- JSON/CSV/PDF export (#243)
- LangGraph agent memory (#213)
- Auth (#182), generation-settings expansions (#220)

- [ ] Empty, in-progress, success, and failure states are clearer and consistent with Instrument panel chrome.
- [ ] Composer and New-chat controls are easier to find and use on desktop and mobile widths.

## User story

As a user, I want Kernector’s real logo and app icons in the Next.js shell and browser chrome so the Instrument panel identity (ADR 0003) reads as one product, not a placeholder letter mark and default favicon.

## Context

Today:

- Shell brand mark is a text **K** in `.kern-brand-mark` (`web/components/shell/AppShell.tsx`).
- Browser tab uses stock `web/app/favicon.ico` (Next.js default).
- No first-party `icon` / `apple-icon` / OG image set aligned with Instrument panel tokens (slate neutrals, restrained teal).

ADR 0003 already names the brand mark as part of shell chrome; this ticket ships the actual mark and icon suite.

## Exact scope

- Add a product logo (SVG preferred) that fits Instrument panel: cool slate + restrained teal; works on light and dark shell surfaces.
- Replace the shell **K** mark with the logo (keep wordmark “Kernector”; remain domain-neutral — no pack branding).
- Ship browser / PWA-style icons: favicon, `icon` sizes, and `apple-icon` (and optional OG/social image if cheap).
- Wire Next.js App Router metadata (`app/icon.*`, `app/apple-icon.*`, and/or `metadata.icons`) so tabs and home-screen bookmarks show Kernector, not the Next default.
- Document where logo/icon sources live (e.g. `web/public/` or `web/app/`) in `web/README.md` Visual direction.

- Redesigning the full Instrument panel token system (already ADR 0003 / `tokens.css`)
- Pack- or connector-specific logos
- Marketing landing / broadsheet branding looks called out as non-goals in ADR 0003

- [ ] Shell brand uses the Kernector logo asset instead of the letter **K**.
- [ ] Favicon / app icons are first-party Kernector assets (no Next.js default).
- [ ] Logo and icons remain legible in light and dark themes.
- [ ] Metadata exposes the icon set so browser tabs and common “Add to Home Screen” paths show Kernector.

## Epic

#124 Next.js presentation foundation and incremental Streamlit migration

## User story

As a user, I want to download grounded chat / test-case transcripts as JSON, CSV, or PDF from the Next.js app so Streamlit retirement (#228) does not remove a shipped export capability.

## Context

Streamlit `render_test_cases_export_actions` offers three downloads that Next.js chat does not:

| Download | Producer | Next.js today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JSON | `presentation/streamlit/cases_export.cases_to_json` | none |
| CSV | `presentation/streamlit/cases_export.cases_to_csv` | none |
| PDF | `cases_pdf_turns` → `composition.conversation_export.build_conversation_pdf` → `infrastructure/export/conversation_transcript_pdf` | none |

`web/components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx` only offers **Copy markdown**. #235 covered chat ask parity, not export. Closed Streamlit work: #181.

#228 Decision 1 recommends keeping `composition/conversation_export.py`, `infrastructure/export/`, and `fpdf2` dormant (delete only Streamlit `cases_export`) and naming this ticket as the known regression in ADR 0004.

## Exact scope

- Expose export of the current conversation (or selected turns / test cases) as JSON, CSV, and PDF from Next.js — client-side generation and/or `/api/v1` endpoints, reusing the dormant PDF stack where practical.
- Keep Markdown / copy-markdown available.
- Sanitize exports: no secrets, raw tool payloads, or leaked prompts.
- Cover each format at the presentation / HTTP boundary with offline tests.
- Update migration-readiness / ADR notes once the gap is closed.

## Exclusions

- Streamlit retirement itself (#228)
- Auth-gated personal export history
- Rewriting domain/application ask logic

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] User can export the current conversation (or selected assistant turn / test cases) as JSON from Next.js.
- [ ] User can export as CSV (sensible columnar projection of role/content/timestamp where available).
- [ ] User can export as PDF (readable transcript; no secrets/tool payloads), preferably via the existing `build_conversation_pdf` path.
- [ ] Markdown / copy-markdown remains available.
- [ ] Tests cover each export path at the presentation boundary without live model calls.
- [ ] Architecture boundaries stay intact (Next talks over HTTP; export builders stay in composition/infrastructure as today).

## Dependencies

- Parent epic **#124**
- Follow-up to Streamlit retirement **#228** (Decision 1 / ADR 0004 known regression)
- Related closed Streamlit export: **#181**
- Not covered by chat parity **#235**

## Definition of Done

- [ ] JSON, CSV, and PDF export usable from Next.js chat / test-case UI
- [ ] Dormant export stack either wired or deliberately replaced with equivalent coverage
- [ ] Tests + architecture gates green; migration-readiness / ADR gap closed
title: Restore test-case / conversation export (JSON, CSV, PDF) in Next.js

## Context

Follow-up from PR #229 / #81 HTTP Problem Details mapping.

HTTP no longer forwards `str(exc)` for `ApplicationValidationError` / `DomainValidationError` (group 9 → 500 fixed operational sentence). The underlying raise idiom still embeds rejected values:

- Dominant pattern: `f"{field} must be X, got {value!r}"`
- ~30 of 45 `ApplicationValidationError` sites and ~12 of 18 `DomainValidationError` sites

Representative sites:

- `application/contracts.py:222` — `history items must be Message, got {item!r}` (conversation content)
- `application/contracts.py:133` — `metadata_filters values must be strings, got {filter_value!r}` (caller input)
- `domain/knowledge.py:120` / `:148` — `chunk must be a DocumentChunk, got {self.chunk!r}` (corpus text)
- `application/manage_documents.py:121` — `generated source_id {source_id!r} already exists`
- `domain/models.py:19` — `role must be one of [...], got {self.role!r}`

Those strings remain on `__cause__` / logs and any future adapter that reuses `str(exc)`.

## User story

As a Kernector engineer, I want validation exceptions to carry safe, field-oriented messages (or typed codes) so logs and any presentation path cannot accidentally leak corpus, history, or filter payloads.

## Exact scope

- Replace `{value!r}` / content-embedding raise messages across `domain/` and `application/` with safe fixed or field-name-only text (or structured error codes).
- Keep enough signal for tests and operators without echoing payloads.
- Update tests that assert on the old verbatim messages.

## Exclusions

- HTTP/Streamlit mapping changes (already aligned for domain validation on the HTTP side).
- New user-facing 4xx exception types for upload size (separate ticket).

## Acceptance criteria

- No domain/application validation raise embeds full `repr` of Message, DocumentChunk, filter values, or document content.
- Offline tests cover representative former leak sites.
- Architecture/error-taxonomy docs note the safe-message convention.
title: Stop embedding rejected values via {value!r} in domain/application validation errors

## Epic

#124 Next.js presentation foundation and incremental Streamlit migration

## User story

As a maintainer, I want Streamlit removed from the repo once Next.js has replaced it as the supported interactive UI so we no longer maintain a dual presentation stack.

## Rationale

ADR `docs/adr/0002-nextjs-presentation-migration.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md` keep Streamlit as a peer adapter during migration. Objective retirement requires feature-parity work, dual-stack CI green (#128), and an explicit product decision. This ticket is that retirement cleanup — not the parity migrations themselves.

## Exact scope

- Confirm product decision that Next.js is the sole supported interactive UI.
- Confirm feature-parity migrations for Streamlit capabilities are complete (chat, upload/ingest, settings/controls, documents, and any remaining Streamlit-only UX).
- Remove `presentation/streamlit/` and Streamlit entrypoints (`main.py` Streamlit run path, README/ops dual-stack Streamlit commands).
- Remove the `streamlit` dependency from `pyproject.toml` / lockfile and any Streamlit-only config or assets.
- Delete or rewrite Streamlit-only tests; keep architecture/boundary coverage for the remaining presentation adapters.
- Update CI (#128 dual-stack workflow) to a Next.js + FastAPI-only presentation stack.
- Update `ARCHITECTURE.md`, ADR #0002 (or a follow-up ADR), and contributor docs so Streamlit is no longer described as a supported peer UI.
- Ensure `uv run` / documented commands no longer require or mention Streamlit.

## Exclusions

- Implementing Next.js feature pages or HTTP feature APIs (those are separate parity tickets)
- Rewriting domain/application logic
- Auth, multi-tenancy, or public deployment hardening beyond what retirement docs require

## Acceptance criteria

- No Streamlit package dependency remains in the production dependency set.
- No `presentation/streamlit` (or equivalent) modules remain in the tree.
- Documented run paths use Next.js + FastAPI only; Streamlit start commands are gone.
- CI no longer runs or documents a Streamlit presentation job.
- Architecture docs and ADR retirement criteria are updated to record the completed decision.
- Full test suite passes without Streamlit.

## Architecture notes

- Per ADR #0002: retirement is **not** part of #124 / #125 definition of done.
- FastAPI under `presentation/http/` remains the HTTP presentation adapter for Next.js.
- Application and domain layers must stay UI-framework-agnostic.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by** feature-parity migrations:
  - #235 Migrate grounded chat to Next.js + FastAPI
  - #236 Migrate document upload/ingest UI to Next.js + FastAPI
  - #237 Migrate provider/model settings controls to Next.js + FastAPI
- **Blocked by #128** (dual-stack CI foundation — complete)
- Also requires an explicit product retirement decision (ADR #0002)
- Parent epic **#124**

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Streamlit code, dependency, and entrypoints removed
- [ ] Docs/ADR/CI updated for single presentation stack
- [ ] Tests and architecture gates green without Streamlit
title: Retire Streamlit presentation after Next.js migration

## Epic

Parent: #9 — Epic: Software Delivery Intelligence domain pack

## User story

As a QA engineer, I want Kernector to analyze project changes against retrieved multi-source project evidence so I can understand their regression impact and generate focused test coverage without relying on the chat prompt alone to contain the project context.

## Rationale

Prompt wording can express the user’s intent and preferred output style, but it cannot establish project understanding by itself.

Kernector needs a dedicated, evidence-grounded capability that compares a change set with the indexed project context, identifies affected behavior and existing tests, explains why they are affected, and exposes unknowns when the available evidence is insufficient.

## Exact scope

- Add a pack-local `software_delivery.regression_impact` tool under `packs/software_delivery/`
- Accept a typed change set containing one or more changed files, diffs, requirements, API/schema changes, configuration changes, or source references
- Accept a retrieved evidence bundle from project sources such as code, tests, SRS, OpenAPI/Swagger, Stories, bugs, and Confluence
- Produce a typed regression-impact report containing:
  - change summary
  - affected components, requirements, APIs, workflows, and existing tests
  - impact reason for every affected item
  - confidence level
  - supporting source references/citations
  - recommended regression-test scope
  - coverage gaps and unknowns
- Preserve provenance from both the change set and retrieved evidence
- Keep contracts and analysis policy inside `packs/software_delivery/`
- Keep shared `ToolRegistry` and `InvokeTool` opaque to the pack-specific payload
- Make the output consumable by test-case generation in #93 and orchestration in #95
- When evidence is missing or contradictory, report uncertainty instead of inventing project relationships

## Exclusions

- Owning repository, Jira, Confluence, or document connectors
- Owning ingestion, indexing, retrieval, or diff acquisition
- Generating the final test cases; #93 owns test-case generation
- Automatically executing tests
- Full dependency-graph or static-analysis engine
- Adding Software Delivery-specific fields to shared core contracts
- Assuming that the model permanently understands the whole project without retrieved evidence

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a valid change set and relevant evidence bundle, when regression-impact analysis runs, then affected project items and a recommended regression-test scope are returned
- Given an affected item, when the output is validated, then its impact reason, confidence, and supporting references are preserved
- Given unrelated evidence, when analysis runs, then it is not reported as impacted without an evidence-backed relationship
- Given incomplete or conflicting evidence, when analysis runs, then unknowns or reduced confidence are returned instead of unsupported conclusions
- Given the impact report is passed to #93, when test generation runs, then focused test cases can be generated without shared core code interpreting the report
- Given generic registry/invocation, when the tool is called, then shared code treats its input and output opaquely
- Given the Software Delivery pack is disabled, when the core boots, then the regression-impact tool is neither imported nor registered

## Technical notes

- Deterministic change/evidence normalization should precede any LLM analysis
- LLM output must be validated against the pack-local typed contract
- LangChain wrappers may exist in infrastructure only
- The user prompt may request the analysis or specify presentation preferences, but evidence retrieval and impact reasoning must be supplied by the application workflow
- #95 should later orchestrate the flow: retrieve evidence → analyze regression impact → generate tests → optionally export Markdown

## Dependencies

- Blocked by #90 — retrieval and citations
- Related to #93 — test-case generation consumes the impact report
- Related to #95 — orchestration selects and chains the capability
- Parent epic #9

## Estimate

M

## Rubric mapping

- Tool calling
- Evidence-grounded reasoning
- Regression-impact analysis
- Multi-source RAG
- Typed structured output

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Pack-local input and output contract tests
- [ ] Sample fixture covering code, requirement/API, and existing-test evidence
- [ ] Affected and unaffected relationship tests
- [ ] Missing/conflicting evidence and uncertainty tests
- [ ] Supporting references preserved end to end
- [ ] Opaque registry/invocation behavior covered
- [ ] Pack-disabled import and registration behavior covered
- [ ] No shared layer imports the Software Delivery pack

## Sprint

title: Software Delivery: analyze regression impact from project changes

## Context

Ticket #122 introduced `DocumentCatalog` with `JsonDocumentCatalog` as the smallest durable registry for the current single-user Streamlit application. JSON is intentionally temporary: it does not provide database transactions, safe multi-process writes, migrations, or suitable concurrency for the planned Next.js/multi-user direction.

This issue is a **follow-up to #122**. Implementation must not begin until an approved **project/workspace/authorization** model exists. **Do not modify code in this task** — tracking and planning only.

## Goal

Add a transactional SQL-backed `DocumentCatalog` adapter without changing application use cases or presentation code.

## Scope

* Implement `SqlDocumentCatalog` behind the existing `DocumentCatalog` port.
* Prefer SQLite initially unless the project’s deployment design requires PostgreSQL.
* Persist every `CatalogDocument` field with uniqueness that includes the **resolved scope identity** from the approved workspace/authorization model (for example project/workspace id plus source identity). Do **not** assume `(source_type, source_id)` is globally unique or safe across workspaces.
* Make `get`, `all`, `upsert`, and `delete` transactional.
* Add schema creation and explicit versioned migrations that encode the resolved scope identity.
* Provide a one-time, idempotent migration from `data/catalog/uploads.json` into the scoped schema.
* Preserve `JsonDocumentCatalog` for local/lightweight usage.
* Select the adapter through configuration; do not branch inside application or presentation.
* Cover restart persistence, duplicate identities within a scope, rollback, concurrent writes, migration success, and migration failure.
* Document when JSON versus SQL should be selected.

## Out of scope

Changes to Chroma retrieval, document chunking, embedding, Next.js UI implementation, and replacing the `DocumentCatalog` port.

**Clarification on tenancy:** designing the project/workspace/authorization model is owned by the future **Project Workspaces and Authorization** epic (issue TBD). This ticket consumes that approved model for schema uniqueness and filters; it does not invent a parallel tenancy design.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Application and presentation work unchanged with either catalog adapter.
2. SQL enforces unique document identity **within the resolved workspace/project scope**.
3. Failed writes roll back without partial catalog state.
4. Concurrent writers do not lose updates.

## Epic

#74 Quality / Evaluation

## User story

As an evaluator, I want an LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation of the RAG pipeline against a fixed dataset and explicit rubrics so I can measure context relevance, faithfulness/groundedness, answer correctness, and citation quality with reproducible evidence—treating judge scores as metrics, not ground truth.

## Rationale

Sprint 2 requires evaluation depth beyond a generic harness. A separate judge story makes RAG quality measurable, comparable across runs, and honest about judge limitations, without conflating automated scores with human truth.

## Exact scope

- Fixed evaluation datasets:
  - A **multi-source core** dataset (generic Kernector retrieval/answer quality across source kinds)
  - A separate **Software Delivery pack** slice (optional pack workflows; not the sole platform dataset)
- Rubric-based LLM-as-a-Judge scoring for:
  - Context relevance (including **cross-source** context relevance)
  - Faithfulness / groundedness
  - Answer correctness
  - Citation accuracy
  - Citation completeness / **source coverage**
- Baseline pass/fail thresholds per metric and/or aggregate gate
- Per-query evidence (scores + short explanations; retrieved context / answer / citations referenced)
- Aggregate metrics (means, pass rates)
- Failure categorisation distinguishing at least: unsupported claims vs retrieval failures vs generation failures, plus **per-source-kind** failure categories where useful
- Deterministic evaluation settings where the judge/provider supports them (e.g. temperature 0 / seed when available)
- Regression comparison against a stored baseline run
- Human review of a sample of cases (documented checklist or sampled IDs)
- Document judge model, version/id, prompt(s), settings, and limitations
- Implementation based on [RAGAS metrics](https://docs.ragas.io/en/stable/concepts/metrics/available_metrics/) and/or [LangSmith RAG evaluation](https://docs.smith.langchain.com/evaluation/tutorials/rag)

## Exclusions

- Treating judge verdicts as ground truth or sole acceptance of product quality
- Showing the judge expected numeric scores, target thresholds, or “correct grade” hints for the case under evaluation
- Asking the judge to evaluate or score its own hidden reasoning / private chain-of-thought
- Replacing human review entirely
- Full production observability platform setup beyond this evaluation command/report
- Expanding tool-calling eval beyond what is needed to exercise the RAG answer path (tool-specific eval remains owned by #102 unless extended here later)
- Treating Story Intelligence as the only evaluation domain

## Judge integrity constraints (mandatory)

- The judge **must not** receive expected scores, target thresholds, or “correct grade” hints for the case under evaluation
- The judge **must not** evaluate or score its own hidden reasoning / private chain-of-thought; only the visible answer, citations, and provided retrieved context (plus dataset fields allowed for the metric)
- Judge output is a **metric signal** used for dashboards, gates, and triage—not authoritative ground truth

## Acceptance criteria

- **Given** the fixed evaluation datasets and a RAG configuration, **when** the evaluation command runs, **then** it produces reproducible JSON and/or CSV results with per-case scores and explanations for context relevance, faithfulness/groundedness, answer correctness, citation accuracy, and citation completeness
- **Given** those per-case results, **when** the run finishes, **then** the output includes summary averages (or equivalent aggregates) and pass/fail against documented baseline thresholds
- **Given** failed or low-scoring cases, **when** results are inspected, **then** unsupported claims and retrieval-versus-generation failures are categorised (not only a single opaque score), including per-source failure labels where applicable
- **Given** cross-source cases, **when** judged, **then** cross-source context relevance and citation/source coverage are reported
- **Given** a baseline from a previous accepted run, **when** a new run regresses below thresholds, **then** the evaluation command exits non-zero
- **Given** the evaluation docs/report, **when** read, **then** judge model/version (or model id), prompt identity/version, settings (including deterministic settings where supported), and limitations are documented
- **Given** the judge prompts/inputs, **when** audited, **then** they do not include expected scores and do not ask the judge to evaluate its own hidden reasoning
- **Given** a documented sample of cases, **when** human review is performed, **then** review notes (or a completed sample checklist) are recorded alongside the automated metrics

## Technical notes

- Prefer composing on RAGAS and/or LangSmith RAG evaluation patterns rather than inventing a one-off opaque scorer
- Reuse the harness entrypoint from #102 where practical; this story owns the judge metrics, thresholds, regression gate, and integrity constraints
- Keep evaluation orchestration in application/infra boundaries consistent with Sprint 2 architecture (no Streamlit-owned scoring logic)
- Offline/fake mode or loud skip when credentials are missing is acceptable for local/CI without secrets, but the primary path must support a real judge run
- Store baseline artifact in-repo or under a documented path for regression comparison

## Dependencies

- Blocked by #90 (Software Delivery analyze-requirements RAG with citations)
- Blocked by #102 (evaluation harness / report scaffolding)
- Parent epic #74
- Relates to / supersedes narrow bonus #103 (faithfulness-only stretch)

M

## Rubric mapping

- Evaluation
- Testing / quality evidence
- Source citations (citation accuracy & completeness)
- Advanced RAG quality (relevance, faithfulness, correctness)
- Bonus/depth evaluation practices (LLM-as-a-Judge used as metric, not truth)

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Fixed core + Software Delivery pack eval datasets committed and versioned
- [ ] Evaluation command documented and runnable
- [ ] JSON and/or CSV outputs include per-case scores + explanations and aggregates
- [ ] Baseline thresholds defined; regression yields non-zero exit
- [ ] Failure categories include unsupported claims, retrieval vs generation, and per-source labels where useful
- [ ] Judge integrity constraints verified (no expected scores; no self-grading of hidden reasoning)
- [ ] Judge model/prompt/settings/limitations documented
- [ ] Human sample review recorded
- [ ] Relationship to #102/#103 clarified in epic notes

## Goal

Deliver a **domain-agnostic reusable knowledge foundation**: generic sources, documents, metadata, chunking, embeddings, retrieval, provenance, citations, collections/workspaces, and document lifecycle management.

## Invariant: source kind ≠ domain pack

Source kinds such as Story, test, Confluence, SRS, OpenAPI/Swagger, code, and future kinds are **complementary evidence sources**. They are not business domains and must not become shared-core entity types. Domain prompts, scoring, and workflows live in optional packs (for example EPIC #9 Software Delivery Intelligence).

A new source kind must not require a new shared-core contract or a new domain tool.

`connector/upload → SourceDocument → retrieval → cited evidence bundle → optional domain tool`

## Goal

Surface **actionable provider errors safely**: the UI consumes typed errors from #98 and maps known categories to curated, user-safe messages so operators can act without opening a terminal—and without rendering raw vendor text.

## Why this matters

Historical `llm.ask` paths replaced failures with misleading generics such as “Failed to connect to OpenRouter”, discarding actionable category information (auth, credits, model unavailable, rate limit, timeout, network).

Example (diagnosed during #33): a privacy/guardrail restriction looked like a connection failure. Users need category-level guidance, not silent swallowing and not raw vendor bodies.

* Presentation maps typed errors (#98) to curated, actionable messages for known categories: authentication failure, insufficient credits, model not available to this account, rate limit, timeout, and genuine network failure.
* Raw vendor bodies, secrets, request headers, stack traces, and untrusted provider text must **never** be rendered in the UI.
* Diagnostic detail may remain only as sanitized `__cause__` retention and/or protected logs—not as primary UI copy.
* Failures remain non-crashing for the presentation path where that pattern already exists; include available safe metadata such as model id/settings when already part of the response contract.

Today the sidebar asks for a provider via a radio button, then shows a separate model selector per provider branch. The provider is an implementation detail of *where* a model runs — it does not need to be a separate decision the user makes first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A single model selector lists all available models across providers.
- [ ] Each option makes its provider obvious (e.g. `OpenRouter · gpt-4o-mini`, `Ollama · llama3.2`).
- [ ] The provider radio button is removed.

- [ ] Model settings from #33 continue to filter correctly by the resolved provider.
- [ ] When Ollama is unreachable or has no models installed, the OpenRouter options still work and the Ollama situation is explained.

## Notes

Known design problems to solve, discussed while implementing #33:

- **Probe cost.** `probe_ollama` currently runs only when Ollama is selected. Building one merged list means probing Ollama on every page load, so users who only use OpenRouter pay the probe latency (and the full timeout when Ollama is not installed). ## Problem
Detection is a brittle substring:

```python
def is_not_interview_prep(reply: str) -> bool:
    return "## Not Interview Pre" in reply
```

That matches a truncated heading and misses variants (extra spaces, case, markdown noise, model typos). False negatives hide the warning; false positives warn on valid prep.

## Goal
Detect the guard section reliably across prompt variants without over-matching.

## Proposed approach
Combine:
1. **Normalize** — lowercase, collapse whitespace, strip markdown emphasis
2. **Regex** — e.g. `^#{1,6}\s*not\s+interview\s+prep\b` (multiline)
3. **Optional fuzzy** — high-threshold match on heading line only (avoid whole-body fuzzy)

Prefer regex + normalize first; add fuzzy only if models drift often.

- [ ] Detects canonical `## Not Interview Prep` from all prompt files
- [ ] Tolerates case / spacing / `#` level / light markdown wrapping
- [ ] Does not treat normal prep content mentioning "interview prep" as the guard
- [ ] Unit tests for positive + negative cases
- [ ] Warning copy stays accurate (today it says "Job Posting" — align with input type if needed)

## Problem
OpenRouter `usage.cost` is not always present or trustworthy for every upstream model (OpenAI/Claude/etc.). Blindly displaying or deriving cost from incomplete OpenRouter fields can produce wrong numbers.

Course brief also points at pricing via `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models`.

## Goal
Prefer authoritative cost; otherwise compute from tokens × known unit prices. Never fabricate cost.

## Proposed approach
1. Prefer `usage.cost` when present and valid (number ≥ 0)
2. Else: `cost = prompt_tokens * prompt_price + completion_tokens * completion_price`
   - Resolve prices from OpenRouter `/api/v1/models` for the selected model id
   - Cache model pricing (TTL)
3. Else: mark cost as unavailable (do not estimate)
4. Ollama: always unavailable / local

- [ ] Fallback: tokens × model pricing from OpenRouter models endpoint
- [ ] Cache pricing lookups
- [ ] If neither cost nor pricing+tokens available → show N/A (no fake $)
- [ ] Unit tests / fixtures for: cost present, cost missing + pricing, both missing, Ollama
- [ ] Caption shows currency clearly (e.g. `$0.0012`)

UI redesign of run meta beyond cost accuracy.
